hypotheses.text: MAU2-related CdLS (CdLS7) exhibits a bimodal phenotypic severity distribution driven by variant mechanism, where truncating/loss-of-function variants causing MAU2 haploinsufficiency lead to a classical CdLS dysmorphic score, whereas in-frame missense/deletion variants impairing heterodimerization yield an attenuated cohesinopathy phenotype clinically indistinguishable from SMC3- or RAD21-related CdLS.
hypotheses.rationale: Parenti et al. (2025/2026) demonstrated that MAU2 truncating mutations cause secondary NIPBL reduction via haploinsufficiency, whereas in-frame variants primarily disturb the NIPBL-MAU2 interface, generating two separate episignatures. Testing whether this divergence maps to distinct clinical severity categories will clarify if 'classical' CdLS presentations can ever arise from MAU2 variants without truncating mechanisms.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 18 individuals with 15 heterozygous MAU2 variants, in-frame variants primarily impaired NIPBL-MAU2 interaction while truncating variants caused haploinsufficiency and NIPBL reduction, accompanied by two MAU2-specific episignatures and phenotypes ranging from classic CdLS to milder presentations.

source.title: Pathogenic variants in the cohesin loader subunit MAU2 lead to a new Cornelia de Lange Syndrome subtype
source.quote: MAU2 in-frame variants predominantly impair NIPBL–MAU2 interaction, whereas truncating variants cause MAU2 haploinsufficiency and lead to NIPBL reduction. Most patients exhibit a DNA methylation profile compatible with the CdLS episignature. We also identified two MAU2 -specific episignatures that reflect variant-dependent molecular consequences. Affected individuals display a wide range of phenotypes, from classic CdLS to milder presentations, with short stature and microcephaly as consistent features.

evidence.text: A Chinese proband with a de novo MAU2 missense variant (p.Arg176Trp) presented with atypical facial features, growth retardation, and reduced exogenous mutant protein levels with altered binding free energy.

source.title: Clinical study and genetic analysis of Cornelia de Lange syndrome caused by a novel MAU2 gene variant in a Chinese boy

hypotheses.text: The clinical phenotypic overlap between CdLS7 and RAD21- or SMC3-related CdLS is so extensive that clinical scoring systems (such as the international CdLS consensus criteria) cannot achieve a positive predictive value greater than 40% for identifying MAU2 without episignature profiling or sequencing.
hypotheses.rationale: Because non-NIPBL cohesinopathies share mild facial gestalt, microcephaly, and cognitive delays while typically lacking severe limb reduction defects, phenotypic criteria alone may not distinguish MAU2 probands from RAD21 or SMC3 probands.

evidence.text: Molecular genetic testing across BRD4, MAU2, NIPBL, RAD21, SMC3, HDAC8, and SMC1A is explicitly recommended to establish diagnosis because individuals with milder CdLS have less severe involvement while sharing non-specific craniofacial and growth features.

source.title: Cornelia de Lange Syndrome - GeneReviews - NCBI - NIH
source.quote: The diagnosis of CdLS is established in a proband with suggestive clinical features and/or a heterozygous pathogenic variant in BRD4, MAU2, NIPBL, RAD21, or SMC3 or a hemizygous or heterozygous pathogenic variant in HDAC8 or SMC1A identified by molecular genetic testing.

hypotheses.text: Severe structural limb reduction defects (including forearm aplasia, absent ulna/radius, and oligodactyly) have a true prevalence of under 5% in CdLS7, such that their presence in a suspected CdLS individual provides high diagnostic likelihood against MAU2 involvement.
hypotheses.rationale: Classical limb deficiencies (e.g. oligodactyly, phocomelia) characterize severe classic NIPBL cases, but cohesin loader partner subunit (MAU2) defects predominantly present with microcephaly, short stature, and craniofacial dysmorphisms without severe structural transverse limb reductions.

evidence.text: Across the 18 individuals reported with pathogenic MAU2 variants, short stature and microcephaly are reported as the consistent major clinical features, while severe structural limb deficiencies are not highlighted as hallmark features.

source.title: Pathogenic variants in the cohesin loader subunit MAU2 underlie a distinct Cornelia de Lange Syndrome subtype
source.quote: Affected individuals display a wide range of phenotypes, from classic CdLS to milder presentations, with short stature and microcephaly as major features.

new_directions.question_text: What are the exact numerator/denominator frequencies of major organ malformations (cardiac defects, diaphragmatic hernia, gastrointestinal malrotation) specifically documented in the 18 MAU2 probands from Parenti et al. (2025/2026)?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying the specific visceral involvement rate will reveal if organ malformation absence can serve as an informative negative predictor for CdLS7 relative to CdLS1.

new_directions.question_text: Does the DNA methylation episignature of MAU2 probands cleanly differentiate MAU2-CdLS7 from SMC3- and RAD21-related CdLS in clinical blood samples?
new_directions.rationale: If clinical dysmorphic features cannot separate CdLS7 from RAD21/SMC3, identifying whether the two MAU2-specific episignatures reliably segregate MAU2 from other cohesinopathies provides the critical definitive diagnostic pipeline.
